newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila committee wants Amari deal "corrected".
newsitem.headline: Manila committee wants Amari deal "corrected".

text.p: A Philippine panel on Thursday endorsed a land deal between the government and the Amari Coastal Development Corp but urged "corrections" in the contract and sought an investigation of three officials who it said may have benefited from the deal.
"The recommendation is to uphold the contract. It was signed by the President and I recommend that everybody respects that signature," Budget Secretary Salvador Enriquez told reporters.
But Enriquez said "some slight, minor provisions (in the contract) should be corrected to firm up the advantages and benefits to the government."
He said the government has to clarify its share on one of the three properties that are covered by the contract.
The deal involves the reclamation and development of 750 hectares of land in Manila.
Amari, a joint venture between Centennial City and and Ital-Thai Development Plc had secured the Manila Bay contract from the government's Public Estates Authority (PEA) last year.

Enriquez said the presidential committee, which he heads, also recommended the investigation of two former officials of PEA and a government lawyer to determine if they have benefitted from the contract.

Last year, Senate president Ernesto Maceda alleged the government entered into a disadvantageous deal since the property was grossly underpriced. He urged for the cancellation of the deal which was already approved by President Fidel Ramos.
Micky Yong, president of Guoco Holdings (Philippines) Inc., earlier defended the deal saying it was not underpriced. Guoco is the parent firm of Centennial.
The valuation of 1,250 pesos per square meter was based on appraisals made by three independent appraisers, Yong said.

Enriquez said the joint venture contract forged by the state-owned firm with the Amari group was fair. "It is fair because we are talking of sharing of the costs and benefits (on the reclamation)," Enriquez said.

"In so far that the government is concerned there is no cost that it will incur. In fact, it is being reimbursed 1.894 billion pesos (on some reclamation work it initially made on the area)," he added.
Enriquez said the government will also get 349 hectares of the land while Amari gets 401 hectares.
"In so far as our committee is concerned...the deal was pursued in earnest to achieve advantage and benefit for the government," he said.
